newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs Friday were seen selling $0.50 per cwt higher, buoyed by Thursday's limit advances in Chicago Mercantile Exchange pork complex futures, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Hog and pork belly futures soared up their daily limits on news that Taiwan had temporarily suspended pork exports because of an outbreak of foot and mouth disease.

Taiwan supplies nearly half of Japan's imported pork and a halt in its exports sparked ideas the U.S. would be a likely supplier, along with Denmark and Canada to fill the void left by Taiwan's absence, analysts said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to interior Iowa and southern Minnesota plants were expected to range $47.50 to $48.00 and Illinois top hog prices at the plant could range $48.00 to $48.50, dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could span$47.00 to $48.00, they said.

Prices also were expected to be underpinned by ideas that fresh pork also would be supported by the Taiwan news, dealers said. Pork prices at midday Thursday were quoted mostly steady with a firm tone, USDA reported. There were 26.0 loads of pork cuts and 12.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
